# John von Neumann
John von Neumann (1903–1957) was a Hungarian-American mathematician and physicist renowned as a polymath who made foundational contributions to mathematics, physics, computer science, economics, and game theory. Born into a wealthy Jewish family in Budapest, he was a child prodigy who entered the University of Budapest and ETH Zurich in 1923, earning degrees in both chemistry and mathematics. He is perhaps best known for his 1932 work, *Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Mechanics* , where he established the rigorous axiomatic framework for quantum theory using Hilbert spaces, and for proving the von Neumann entropy, which remains central to quantum information theory.
Von Neumann revolutionized several fields, including the axiomatization of set theory (proposing the axiom of foundation), the development of ergodic theory, and the invention of the von Neumann architecture for stored-program computers, which underpins modern computing. He co-founded game theory with Oskar Morgenstern and invented the minimax theorem and the merge sort algorithm. His intellectual work extended to economics, where he formulated the model of an expanding economy and contributed to linear programming. A founding figure in the Manhattan Project, he designed the implosion mechanism for the plutonium core of the atomic bomb. Following the war, he served as a key advisor to the U.S. government on nuclear weapons, ICBMs, and missile defense. He died of cancer in 1957 at age 53, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most influential scientists of the 20th century.
